title: This Songbird Walks Underwater to Hunt, With a Built-In Swim Mask
subject: american dipper

scenes.text: A songbird walks along the bottom of rivers. On purpose.
The American dipper is sparrow-sized. It dives into mountain streams and walks the bottom, wings beating to stay down.
It flips over pebbles and debris, hunting insect larvae and fish eggs.
A see-through third eyelid works like a swim mask. Scales close over its nostrils.
Dives last about 5 to 15 seconds. Then it pops up and bobs, sometimes once a second.
A waterproof oil gland keeps its feathers dry. The river isn't empty. Something small is walking on the bottom.

description:
The American dipper is a sparrow-sized songbird that walks underwater to hunt.
A clear third eyelid acts like a swim mask, scales close over its nostrils, and an oil gland waterproofs its feathers. Most dives last 5 to 15 seconds.
Have you ever spotted one bobbing on a river rock?
first_comment: Dippers are also called water ouzels. Would you rather swim like a fish or walk the riverbed like this bird?
